page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.32xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.g7 family. It is equipped with 128 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs, utilizing Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance features a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is disabled or configured to provide one thread per physical core. It is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance does not include local storage, requiring all storage operations to utilize network-attached block storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, which facilitates high-throughput communication with external storage volumes and other network resources. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor. There are no hardware accelerators or GPUs integrated into this configuration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7.32xlarge offers high resource density for workloads requiring massive parallel processing without the overhead of hyperthreading. The dedicated core allocation ensures predictable compute performance. It is designed for large-scale enterprise applications, web serving fleets, containerized microservices, and distributed databases that rely on network-attached storage and require a balanced ratio of compute power to memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.32xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 128 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance is designed for workloads requiring high parallel processing capacity and predictable compute performance, such as enterprise applications, large-scale web serving, and containerized deployments.
